task.description: Review the diff for REQ-001a (git diff master...HEAD on branch feature/WF02-REQ-001a) per WF-02 Step 2b. FRONTEND-DEV reported 4 deliberate deviations from the design in its handoff (handoffs/WF02-REQ-001a/step-02-frontend-dev.json result section) — read that handoff's full result to see them, and judge each on its merits rather than treating any deviation as automatically disqualifying: (1) proxy.ts placed at src/proxy.ts instead of repo root, because Next resolves the middleware/proxy file relative to the app directory's parent, not true repo root — verify this claim yourself if you can, or treat it as a plausible engineering fact worth spot-checking rather than blocking on; (2) NextIntlClientProvider added around {children} in the locale layout, not in the original design's file tree, needed because LocaleSwitcher is a Client Component using useLocale/usePathname which throw without it; (3) 'checked in both light/dark theme' was reported as not applicable because globals.css has no data-theme split at all (single fixed dark palette) — verify this is true by reading globals.css yourself, don't take it on faith; (4) mobile/desktop viewport was checked only statically (no media query on .lang in globals.css) rather than visually, because no browser tool was available to the implementing agent — you have the same tool constraints, so assess whether this is an acceptable verification gap for this step or something that must block. Also run the standard review: check the diff against docs/Design system for AI agents/readme.md (tokens, spacing, component classes, copy casing), docs/agents/anti-patterns.md (empty today, so trivially clear), scope (does the change do only what REQ-001a asked, no more/less), and consistency with docs/agents/decisions/ (only 0001, unrelated).
acceptance_criteria: git diff master...HEAD read directly, not just the FRONTEND-DEV handoff summary
Each of the 4 reported deviations explicitly judged, not silently accepted or silently flagged without a verdict
Scope check confirms no unrelated changes bundled into this diff beyond what REQ-001a's acceptance criteria require
If a genuine violation is found, FAIL with the specific file/line and rule violated; otherwise PASS, noting any non-blocking observations for the record

result.summary: Read git diff master...HEAD directly (24 files, +1520/-78; 15 files touched outside handoffs/docs, listed exhaustively below) rather than trusting FRONTEND-DEV's summary. Diff scope is exactly REQ-001a's five bullets and nothing else: dependency (package.json/package-lock.json add next-intl@4.13.7), routing restructure (src/app/page.tsx+layout.tsx -> src/app/[locale]/page.tsx [pure rename, similarity 100%] + src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx [new, async, dynamic <html lang>, generateMetadata]), proxy (src/proxy.ts, new), message catalogs (messages/ru.json, messages/uz.json, matching key sets, uz.ogLocale correctly uz_UZ not duplicated), switcher (src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx new + Nav.tsx 8-line edit swapping the static <div class=lang> block for <LocaleSwitcher/>), and the required accompanying CSS selector rename (.lang span -> .lang a, one line, same declaration block, same values, per design doc section 3 recommendation (a)). src/app/health/route.ts, Dockerfile, ci-cd.yml, deploy.sh and all other deploy infra are untouched, confirming the design's explicit constraint was honored. No raw hex/oklab or spacing values were added anywhere in the diff -- the only globals.css change is the selector-target rename, same var(...) declarations, no new rule. Checked against docs/Design system for AI agents/readme.md: per the accepted WF-01/design-gate decision, this component intentionally stays on globals.css's bespoke classes rather than the documented OKLCH tokens, so token/type-scale/spacing/component-class rules from that doc do not apply to this diff's CSS; verified the diff introduces no new class, no new value, and no copy that violates the doc's casing/vocabulary rules (switcher labels are RU/UZ mono uppercase codes, consistent with existing convention, not new copy). docs/agents/anti-patterns.md has no entries to check against (confirmed by reading it). No conflict with docs/agents/decisions/0001 (pipeline-scope only, unrelated). Independently re-ran npm run lint (4 problems, 0 errors, 4 warnings, all pre-existing @next/next/no-img-element + one unused-var in files this diff never touches -- confirmed by cross-referencing warning file paths against the diff's file list) and npm run build (exit 0, Turbopack build, route table shows /[locale] and /health as dynamic and 'f Proxy (Middleware)' registered, matching FRONTEND-DEV's reported output) -- both independently verified, not taken on faith. Judged FRONTEND-DEV's 4 reported deviations on their merits: (a) src/proxy.ts vs repo-root proxy.ts -- verified directly against node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/proxy.md, which states verbatim: 'Create a proxy.ts (or .js) file in the project root, or inside src if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as pages or app.' Since this project's app dir is src/app, src/proxy.ts is exactly the documented-correct location, not merely a plausible empirical workaround as FRONTEND-DEV framed it -- the claim is correct and actually more solidly grounded than FRONTEND-DEV's own justification suggested. No violation. (b) NextIntlClientProvider added around {children} -- verified against the installed package's actual type declarations (node_modules/next-intl/dist/types/shared/NextIntlClientProvider.d.ts, exported from both react-client and react-server indices) and use-intl's runtime source (node_modules/use-intl/dist/esm/production/react.js): useLocale()/usePathname() resolve via a context created by IntlProvider and throw `new Error(...)` when no provider is present in the tree. This is a genuine, necessary wiring requirement for LocaleSwitcher's client hooks to function, not scope creep -- it adds no new file, only a required wrapper already implicit in next-intl's documented client-hook contract. No violation. (c) 'no data-theme split' claim -- read src/app/globals.css in full myself: zero occurrences of `data-theme` anywhere in the file, single fixed :root palette (--bg, --fg, --primary etc as raw hex), confirming the claim is accurate and the light/dark self-review criterion genuinely does not apply to this component as designed. No violation. (d) no visual viewport verification -- assessed as an acceptable gap for this step: REVIEWER has the same lack of a browser/viewport tool as FRONTEND-DEV, and FRONTEND-DEV did perform the correct fallback check available without one (grepped globals.css for media-query overrides on .lang at both the 980px and 620px breakpoints and found none, meaning the switcher inherits the same layout at all widths with no responsive-specific risk introduced by this diff). I independently re-read the full globals.css media-query blocks (lines 247-263) and confirm .lang/.lang a/.lang .on are not referenced in either @media block, so no breakpoint-dependent regression is plausible from this change. This is the same standard of verification I can perform, so I accept it as sufficient for this gate rather than blocking on a tool constraint neither role can resolve. No violation. Overall verdict: PASS. Non-blocking notes for the record: (1) the accessible-label question for the switcher wrapper (design doc open question 5) remains unresolved -- acceptable since no CONTENT-BA copy exists and the design explicitly left omission as the conservative default; (2) generateStaticParams for [locale] (open question 4) remains unimplemented, acceptable since no acceptance criterion requires it.
